brief.offer: Paid search campaigns for privacy-focused software products

facts.claim: Plausible Analytics is an independent, open source analytics company based in the EU.
facts.excerpt: Plausible Analytics is an independent, open source analytics company based in the EU.

facts.claim: The product is privacy-focused: it does not use cookies and does not collect personal data.
facts.excerpt: We do not use cookies and we do not collect personal data.

facts.claim: The company reached $1 million in annual recurring revenue in 2022 and says it has continued to grow profitably without outside funding.
facts.excerpt: Plausible crossed $1 million in annual recurring revenue in 2022 and has continued to grow as a profitable, independently operated company.

facts.claim: Plausible says it has never spent money on advertising, affiliates, or paid endorsements and grows through word of mouth.
facts.excerpt: We have never spent a cent on advertising, affiliates or paid endorsements. Plausible grows because people recommend it when they have no reason to other than that it works.

facts.claim: The white-label model lets each customer have their own dashboard and site data inside the vendor’s interface.
facts.excerpt: Customers stay inside your interface and see a dashboard that already feels familiar.
facts.source_title: White label web analytics for SaaS platforms and website builders | Plausible Analytics

facts.claim: Plausible supports multi-tenant integrations where a backend provisions one site per customer and sends each customer’s events to the matching site.
facts.excerpt:
Provision one site for each customer
   2. Send each customer’s events to the matching site
   3. Show the analytics inside your product
facts.source_title: White label web analytics for SaaS platforms and website builders | Plausible Analytics

facts.claim: Plausible says it serves thousands of customers and new trials, helped by a minimal product and detailed documentation.
facts.excerpt: The product itself being minimal and easy to use makes it possible for us to serve thousands of customers and new trials without being overwhelmed with messages.
facts.source_title: How we scaled support for 4,000+ subscribers and 1,000+ monthly trials (without dedicated support personnel) | Plausible Analytics

research.website_note: The plausible.io site is described in multiple official results as Plausible Analytics’ own website and product site.

dropped.claim: Plausible offers a white-label analytics product for SaaS platforms, website builders, marketplaces, and hosting services.
dropped.excerpt: White label web analytics for SaaS platforms and website builders | Plausible Analytics

strategy.observation: Plausible’s product is explicitly privacy-focused: it does not use cookies and does not collect personal data.
strategy.offer_link: A paid search program could help capture people already looking for cookie-free, GDPR-friendly, or privacy-first analytics tools, which is a natural match for Plausible’s positioning if they wanted a new acquisition channel.
hypotheses: They may be considering a channel beyond word-of-mouth to reach intent-driven buyers.
There may be search demand around privacy-focused analytics that Plausible could convert efficiently.
They may be open to a paid acquisition test even though they have historically avoided advertising.
strategy.angle: Plausible’s privacy-first analytics product is well positioned to intercept searchers looking for cookie-free, GDPR-friendly tools.
strategy.fit_reason: The privacy-first positioning makes paid search plausible, but Plausible says it has grown through word of mouth and has never spent on advertising, so this would be a new channel rather than an obvious existing priority.

draft.subject: Cookie-free search demand
draft.body:
Plausible’s product is built to avoid cookies and personal data collection.

I run paid search campaigns for privacy-focused software. It can be a clean way to catch people already looking for cookie-free or GDPR-friendly analytics.

If you ever want to test that demand, would a small search campaign around those terms be worth setting up?
